findings.title: The brand describes itself differently in different places on the same page
findings.evidence: 3 pair(s) of self-descriptions on the homepage share little vocabulary; the Organization schema description and the meta description overlap by only 6% ("Loom is the video messaging platform for work. It enables a more effec" vs "Best free online screen recording tool with advanced video editing and").

descriptions.meta description: Best free online screen recording tool with advanced video editing and video storage trusted by over 22 million people and easy sharing from Loom.com.
descriptions.og:description: Best free online screen recording tool with advanced video editing and video storage trusted by over 22 million people and easy sharing from Loom.com.
descriptions.twitter:description: Best free online screen recording tool with advanced video editing and video storage trusted by over 22 million people and easy sharing from Loom.com.
descriptions.Organization schema description: Loom is the video messaging platform for work. It enables a more effective, expressive way of communicating through videos that are instantly ready to record, share and watch anywhere.

findings.mechanism: These fields are read by different consumers, and together they form the brand's self-description. When they disagree, a system has no single authoritative account of what the brand is; it either hedges, blends them into something the brand never said, or prefers a third-party description that at least appears consistently.

suggested_action.summary: Write one canonical description of the organisation and use it in every one of these fields.
how: Agree a single sentence describing what the organisation is, who it serves and where.
Use it verbatim in the meta description, og:description, twitter:description and the Organization schema `description`.
Use the same sentence in off-site profiles - LinkedIn, Crunchbase, directories - so the description the wider web repeats matches the site.
suggested_action.verify: Re-run check ENT-001 and confirm it no longer fires.

findings.title: The site publishes few verifiable facts about the organisation itself
findings.evidence: Across 6 sampled page(s): no About page was found; no founding date, headquarters or 'based in' statement appears in the text.
findings.mechanism: A claim repeated consistently across many independent sources is treated as reliable; a claim that exists in one place is fragile. Before the wider web can repeat anything about an organisation, the organisation has to state it somewhere quotable. With no founding date, location, scale or named figures published, there is nothing for journalists, directories or assistants to corroborate - so the brand has no verifiable substance to attach to its name.

suggested_action.summary: Publish a facts page: what the organisation is, when and where it was founded, its scale, and who leads it.
how: Create or expand an About page stating founding year, headquarters location, legal entity name, leadership and size, in plain sentences.
Publish named, dated figures the press and analysts can cite - customers served, locations, headcount - and keep them current.
Add a press or newsroom page carrying the same facts in a form journalists can lift.
Mirror the same facts in Organization schema (foundingDate, address, numberOfEmployees, founder) so they are machine-readable as well as readable.
suggested_action.verify: Re-run check ENT-006 and confirm it no longer fires.
